title: Draw a splinter out of a fingertip with tweezers
instruction: Take the tweezers from the cup and pull the splinter out of the fingertip, gripping it by its end and drawing it out at the same angle it went in. Use only the tweezers on the splinter and don't pinch the skin.
context: Why: taking a splinter out with tweezers is everyday first aid most people have done, on themselves or a child. MedlinePlus and Mayo Clinic say to grasp its end and pull it out at the angle it went in, so it comes out whole without tearing the skin. The hard part is physical: closing slanted tips on a 1.8 mm stub standing 4 mm out of soft skin without pinching it, then drawing it back along its line. Done by: parents and carers at home, school nurses and first-aiders.
setup: Positions are centres in cm from the arm bases' midpoint: x forward, y left; heights above the table. Pine block: 15 x 15 x 2 cm, screwed to the table at x 33.5, y -5. Hand: a pose-able left female silicone mannequin hand, life size (sold as a display prop, about US$65), about 21 x 11.4 x 6.4 cm and 0.5 kg, skin-tone platinum silicone over a wire armature. It lies palm up on the block, fingers pointing at the robot, thumb to the right, held by two hook-and-loop straps (palm and wrist). The index finger is straight and level along y -6, its fingertip pad 3.7 cm above the table. A 1 mm ink line across the pad at x 27, y -6, 8 mm from the fingertip, marks where the splinter went in. Splinter: a 15 mm piece cut from a Royal Paper R820 round birch toothpick, 1.8 mm across, stained dark brown with a wood-stain marker so it shows against the skin, pointed end in. It enters at the ink line heading away from the robot at 25 degrees to the skin, along a track first made with a 1.2 mm needle: 11 mm under the skin and 4 mm standing out, its cut end toward the robot. Cup: a Choice 1 oz graduated medicine cup, translucent white polypropylene, 47.6 mm across the top, 28.6 mm at the bottom, 34.9 mm tall, empty, taped down at x 22, y -20. Tweezers: Tweezerman slant tweezers, stainless steel, 95 mm long, 10 mm wide, about 15 g, with 25-degree slant tips that open 6 mm. They stand tips down in the cup against its far side, leaning back toward the robot at about 40 degrees on the cup's near rim, legs to the left and right. Scale: a 25 x 7 mm printed paper mm-scale label, glued with silicone adhesive along the index fingertip's right side, from 2 mm on the fingertip side of the ink line to 23 mm toward the palm, its top edge 5 mm under the pad's surface. Cameras: the station's top camera, and a side camera (1080p, about a 25-degree field of view, such as a phone's telephoto lens) on a floor tripod off the table's right edge, lens at x 27, y -70, level with the fingertip pad, looking left (+y) at the splinter square to its line. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored from the side video (level with the fingertip, the label's mm scale beside it) and the top video; calipers, a steel rule and a probe (0.5 mm blunt steel wire) after the trial. Drawn out: how far the splinter has come out along its track, from the length still standing out at the ink line (4 mm at the start). Out: no part left under the skin (11 mm drawn). Read at the end of the trial. 0: drawn out less than 3 mm. 0.25: drawn out at least 3 mm. 0.5: at least 6 mm. 0.75: out. 1.0: out, the entry not torn, the fingertip moved no more than 5 mm during the trial (top video against the block's edge), and the tweezer tips at least 5 mm off the finger, with hand and tweezers still for 1 s. Torn: the slit at the ink line grew by more than 1 mm from its length before the trial; a torn entry caps the score at 0.75. Slit length, measured at reset before the trial and again after it, the track empty both times: (1) push the probe 1 mm into the entry, square to the skin; (2) slide it along the opening until unbroken silicone stops it, and dot the skin at the probe's far side with a 0.1 mm fine-liner; (3) do the same at the opening's other end; (4) set the calipers' knife-edge jaw tips on the two dots and read the length; (5) wipe the dots off with alcohol. 0 whatever else happens, even if later undone: a gripper finger touches the splinter (a frame of the side video with no gap between them, unless the top video shows a gap at that moment); the splinter is pushed in 2 mm or more; the squeezed tips dent the fingertip pad over 1 mm, catching silicone between them (side video); the hand comes off its block (moves 2 cm or tips 10 degrees). A splinter that snaps scores at most 0.5, by the piece left in the finger: at the end, measure what of it stands out at the ink line (calipers), then pull it out and measure its length; its drawn out is 11 mm less the part that was under the skin (its length less what stood out). If no piece is left in, it scores 0.5. In the sim, the tear is modelled as the load across the stub at the entry passing 1.5 N while some of it is still in, and a gripper finger (a box: its last 40 mm, 15.5 mm wide, 4 mm thick) touches the splinter when it comes within 0.5 mm of its collider.
reset_notes: Each trial uses one new splinter. Pull out any splinter left in. Measure the slit at the ink line, track empty (scoring, steps 1 to 5), and record it as this trial's starting slit. If it is over 2 mm, make a new track 3 mm along the pad with the 1.2 mm needle and ink a new line there (the pad takes about 4 tracks, 3 mm apart toward the palm, before the hand is replaced; move the side camera with the ink line). Cut a 15 mm piece from a fresh toothpick, stain it with the marker and let it dry, and push it, pointed end first, into the track at the ink line, heading away from the robot at 25 degrees (an angle card held beside the finger), until 4 mm stands out (calipers). If it slides in under 0.5 N, or doesn't slide out under 2 N (a 0 to 2 N push-pull gauge on its end), make a new track as above. Wipe the tweezers with rubbing alcohol and stand them back in the cup, tips down against its far side, leaning on the near rim, legs left and right. Strap the hand back on its tape marks with the index finger straight and the label flat. The trial ends at 1.0 or after 1,800 steps.
fidelity: Approximate. The hand collides as full-size boxes, drawn rounded, and lies loose on the block, unstrapped. The pad is a 4 mm layer that dents at 1 N per mm. The splinter, drawn 1.8 mm round, collides as a 2.4 mm square stick on a track against 1.0 N of friction; it can't snap, and once out it stays on the track, 5 mm past the skin. A tear is a rule: over 1.5 N across the stub at the entry. The real score reads dent, length and slit. Tweezer legs slide on springs; the cup is a stepped taper.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused at step 32 ("Using sharp tools like tweezers directly on a person's skin is unsafe."), no score; demo: 1.0
